headlines.title: What Is Going On With Regeneron Stock?
headlines.summary: Regeneron Pharmaceuticals (REGN) stock currently trades at 17.6 times earnings. That represents a notable discount to the 21.5 multiple of the median S&P 500 company. The shares have lost 4.1% over the past six months, trailing the 15.7% return of the broader index. Over twelve months, however, the stock returned 27% against the index's 17.1%. A valuation this low suggests investors are either overlooking a sound drug maker or pricing in underlying problems.

headlines.title: Is Biohaven (BHVN) Quietly Recasting Its Oncology Strategy Through Deeper Ties With Regeneron?
headlines.summary: In September 2026, Biohaven Ltd. announced a clinical supply agreement with Regeneron Pharmaceuticals to test BHV-1530 in combination with cemiplimab (Libtayo) in patients with solid tumors, following earlier monotherapy and preclinical data suggesting potential synergy with Anti-PD-1 therapy.

headlines.title: Regeneron Co-Founder on R&D, Data and Omics
headlines.summary: George Yancopoulos, Regeneron president and chief scientific officer, shares the difference between how his company invests compared to their competitors, the importance of data for finding the next breakthrough drug and how to out-innovate China.

headlines.title: Expanded Sanofi Alliance And New Pipeline Data Could Be A Game Changer For Regeneron (REGN)
headlines.summary: In early October 2026, Regeneron Pharmaceuticals reported new clinical data across oncology and obesity programs and expanded its long-running antibody alliance with Sanofi, which includes US$1.00 billion upfront and potential future milestone payments worth up to US$7.00 billion.

headlines.title: Regeneron Showcases Advances in Care Across Several Cancers and Cancer-associated Complications at ESMO 2026
headlines.summary: Late-breaking Phase 3 C-POST data provide longer-term survival outcomes for adjuvant Libtayo® (cemiplimab) in high-risk cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (CSCC) after surgery and radiation Final Phase 2 analysis explores potential of Libtayo before surgery (neoadjuvant treatment) for patients with resectable CSCC New data explore inhibition of Factor XI for cancer-associated thrombosis, a leading cause of cancer death, where bleeding risk limits use of anticoagulants TARRYTOWN, N.Y., Oct.

description: Regeneron Pharmaceuticals, Inc. discovers, invents, develops, manufactures, and commercializes medicines to treat various diseases worldwide. The company develops product candidates to treat eye, allergic and inflammatory, cardiovascular, metabolic, neurological, infectious, and rare diseases; and cancer, hematologic conditions. It also offers EYLEA injections for wet age-related macular degeneration and diabetic macular edema; myopic choroidal neovascularization; diabetic retinopathy; neovascular glaucoma; retinopathy of prematurity; Dupixent injection to treat atopic dermatitis and asthma; Libtayo injection for metastatic or locally advanced cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma; Praluent injection to treat heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HoFH); and Kevzara solution for rheumatoid arthritis. It has license and collaboration agreement with Bayer for the development and commercialization of EYLEA 8 mg and EYLEA; Alnylam Pharmaceuticals, Inc. to discover, develop, and commercialize RNAi therapeutics for diseases by addressing therapeutic disease targets expressed in the eye and central nervous system; Intellia Therapeutics, Inc. to advance CRISPR/Cas9 gene-editing technology for in vivo therapeutic development for therapies focused on neurological and muscular diseases; Hansoh Pharmaceuticals Group Company Limited to acquire development and commercial rights for HS-20094, a dual GLP-1/GIP receptor; and Tessera Therapeutics, Inc. develops and commercializes TSRA-196, an investigational gene editing therapy for Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency. Additionally, the company has a strategic collaboration with Telix Pharmaceuticals Limited to develop and commercialize radiopharmaceutical therapies. It also has a strategic collaboration with CytomX Therapeutics, Inc. to create conditionally-activated bispecific cancer therapies. The company was incorporated in 1988 and is based in Tarrytown, New York.
